newsitem.title: USA: Chrysler sales edge up 1.1 percent in December.
newsitem.headline: Chrysler sales edge up 1.1 percent in December.

text.p: Chrysler Corp. squeezed out a 1.1 percent increase in total vehicle sales in December to finish the year with record sales of 2.45 million cars and trucks, the automaker said Friday.

Bolstered by strong sales of minivans, pickup trucks and sport/utility vehicles, Chrysler said its 1996 sales totalled 2,450,826 vehicles, nearly 13 percent above the 1995 total of 2,164,343 units. It broke the company's previous annual sales record of 2,208,057 units, set in 1988.

Chrysler said its December sales of North American-built vehicles rose 5.4 percent to 57,602 units from 54,673 a year earlier, but December light truck sales dipped 0.2 percent to 122,202 units from 122,468 unites.
For the full year, Chrysler's domestic car sales rose 6.6 percent to 827,941 units from 771,357 units a year ago.
Light truck sales posted a 16.7 percent gain to 1,618,193 units in 1996 from 1,378,163 in 1995.

Chrysler's import car sales, reflecting the discontinuation of models built by Mitsubishi Motor Corp. and imported from Japan, fell 68.6 percent for the full year to 4,692 cars from 14,823. Chrysler sold no imported cars in the United States during December.
James Holden, Chrysler executive vice president for sales and marketing, said Chrysler's U.S. sales were up more than 60 percent since 1991, with sales to retail customers nearly doubled.
"We have been consistently outperforming the industry in sales and our share of the market has grown substantially," Holden said in a statement.
"We plan to continue to capture customers from our competitors. And we expect the strong loyalty of Chrysler customers to become even stronger."
General Motors Corp. was scheduled to report its December sales later Friday. Ford Motor Co. was due to report its year-end sales on Monday.
Chrysler's stock added 50 cents to $34.625 in midday trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
